cds.text: Share ideas about stories, poems and images, reflecting on similar or different experiences, using First Nations Australian and wider Australian and world texts
Discuss how language and images create characters, settings and events in these literary texts
Discuss how characters and settings are connected in these literary texts
Respond to stories and share feelings and thoughts about events and characters
Discuss literary texts and share responses by connecting them to students' own experiences
Identify features of literary texts, such as characters and settings, and give reasons for personal preferences
Recognise types of literary texts and their features, including events, characters, beginnings and endings
Discuss plot, character and setting as features of stories
Discuss the characters and settings of a range of texts and how language presents them in different ways
Explore and replicate rhythms and sound patterns in poems, rhymes and songs
Listen to and discuss poems, chants, rhymes and songs; imitate and invent sound patterns, including alliteration and rhyme
Identify, reproduce and experiment with rhythmic sound and word patterns in poems, chants, rhymes or songs
Retell and adapt familiar literary texts through play, performance, images or writing
Orally retell or adapt a familiar story using plot, characters, vocabulary and structure through role-play, writing, drawing or digital tools
Create and edit literary texts by adapting structures and language features of familiar texts through drawing, writing, performance and digital tools

sentences.text: {{S}} understands how language evokes emotions and describes characters through their traits and actions.
{{S}} identifies and applies themes in various texts.
{{S}} identifies themes in narratives and applies them when creating {{pos}} own texts.

{{S}} identifies main ideas in narratives and uses these when creating original texts.
{{S}} identifies words and phrases that are used to persuade the reader.
{{S}} identifies themes in narratives and connects with key ideas in a variety of stories.
{{S}} identifies how advertisements are organised and describes features of both fiction and non-fiction texts.
{{S}} describes features of fiction and non-fiction texts and how pictures and words contribute to meaning.
{{S}} recognises how authors create characters and structure stories to engage the reader.
{{S}} shows enjoyment when listening to stories and expresses {{pos}} opinions about characters and events.
{{S}} joins in class discussions about stories to identify the beginning, middle and end.
{{S}} names {{pos}} favourite stories and characters in class discussions.
{{S}} enjoys creative language such as sound words and rhymes.
{{S}} tries creative language in {{pos}} own telling and writing.
{{S}} writes related sentences to create stories.
{{S}} talks about how stories build feelings and compares characters in different texts.
{{S}} finds figurative language, wordplay and symbols in texts.
{{S}} uses figurative language or wordplay in {{pos}} own writing.
{{S}} uses {{pos}} experiences to help {{o}} understand and form opinions about a text.
{{S}} identifies how authors use words in unexpected ways to make stories interesting.
{{S}} describes how a character's choices affect a storyline.
{{S}} identifies the difference between language that expresses opinion versus fact and uses this knowledge to describe the purpose of a text.

rows.newText: {{S}} shares ideas about stories, poems and pictures and says how they link to {{pos}} own experiences.
{{S}} shares feelings and thoughts about the events and characters in a story.
{{S}} recognises the characters, events and endings in familiar stories.
{{S}} joins in rhymes, songs and poems and repeats their rhythm and sound patterns.
{{S}} retells a familiar story through play, drawing or performance.
{{S}} discusses how words and pictures show the characters, settings and events in a story.
{{S}} describes a character or setting using ideas from the words and pictures.
{{S}} shares {{pos}} response to a story by linking it to {{pos}} own life.
{{S}} discusses the plot, characters and setting of a story.
{{S}} listens to poems, chants and songs and makes up new lines using sound patterns.
{{S}} retells a familiar story aloud using the plot, characters and some of the story words.
{{S}} changes part of a familiar story and tells it in {{pos}} own way.
{{S}} explains how the characters and settings in a story are connected.
{{S}} identifies characters and settings in a story and gives reasons for {{pos}} response.
{{S}} describes how the language of a text presents its characters and settings.
{{S}} writes a poem or chant that copies the rhythm and sound patterns of ones {{s}} has read.
{{S}} creates and edits a short story by adapting the structure and language of a familiar text.
